extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DoD contracting officers and procurement personnel involved in CITA/A-76 service contracting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for preparing solicitations, Statements of Work, cost comparisons, and conducting procurements under the Commercial/Industrial Type Activities (CITA) program and OMB Circular A-76 within Navy/DoD contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW) & surveillance plan linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: The preparation of the SOW and the surveillance plan go hand-in-hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desired outcomes, methods of assessing performance, and criteria to determine acceptable or deficient performance are key ingredients of any well prepared Statement of Work. Functional activity personnel should be involved early in SOW development to improve quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of centralized SOWs and existing specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional activity personnel should be made aware of the existence of centralized SOWs for many functional areas currently being compiled by CNM and DOD Service Contract Group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized outlines and specifications can be of significant value; common deficiencies in specification preparation (e.g., Enclosure (6) to Reference 51) should be provided to activities as guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain integrity of competitive bidding system
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide for equitable and consistent treatment of all interested persons, groups, and organizations; maintain overall integrity of the competitive bidding system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even the appearance of possible compromise can lead to severe criticism. Procedures and safeguards should be established to assure integrity and objectivity throughout the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict access to Government in-house cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel involved in contracting and evaluation should have no access to the Government in-house cost estimate until the most favorable offer to the Government has been determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting the number of personnel who see the in-house estimate reduces risk of compromise. Violations (e.g., multiple contracting office reps seeing estimate before determination) undermine the process and complicate audit justification for adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of Conduct acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Task Group personnel should review and sign Standards of Conduct Statement per DOD Directive 5500.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task Group Chairperson must advise members on maintaining integrity/objectivity and establish procedures to ensure compliance (Air Force example recommends signatures). Contracting Officer may assist or take initiative to implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of cost comparison clause for formally advertised solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitation must notify bidders that the solicitation is subject to a Government cost comparison and explain distribution/availability of the in-house cost estimate and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clause text includes: provision that in-house cost estimate will be provided at bid opening or as practicable, three-year cost-comparison basis and straightlining for shorter bids, five-workday wait after bid opening for review, and availability of completed cost comparison after award or cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of cost comparison clause for negotiated solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerers are placed on notice that the solicitation is subject to a Government cost comparison and describes sealed submission/opening of the Government's in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The in-house estimate is submitted sealed prior to receipt of priced proposals, opened publicly after most favorable offer determined, considered a 'proposal' for Late Proposals clause, five-workday review period for appeals, and three-year projection methodology described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year cost-comparison methodology (evaluation only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government cost comparison is based on a three-year cost estimate for averaging atypical first-year conversion costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contractor bid is for one year, it will be straightlined for years 2 and 3; government costs similarly straightlined except known changes (excluding inflation) adjusted. Activities encouraged to contract for three-year periods but evaluation period is not binding on bidders/offerors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-priced options to mitigate buy-ins
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations should provide for pre-priced options for out-year performance to prevent buy-ins and broaden period for cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options provide continuity and reduce disruption, but conflict may exist with DAR preference for resolicitation for annual requirements. Pre-priced options may still be required where appropriate, subject to Service Contract Act effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service Contract Act (SCA) impact on option-year evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: When SCA mandates redetermination of labor rates, contractor option-year prices do not necessarily reflect true future costs; cost comparison may be limited to one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where SCA mandates redetermination for covered contractor employees, NAVSUP revised guidance to make cost comparison for one year only for solicitations released after Oct 1, 1979; pre-priced options still required where SCA not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required general contract clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations must include clauses relating to equal employment opportunity, veterans preference, minimum wages and fringe benefits, and OFPP wage-busting policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These clauses are normally included in service contracts and the Circular requires their inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of displaced employees to priority consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Include clause requiring contractor to give employees displaced by conversion the right of refusal for employment openings for which they may be qualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required by the Circular to protect displaced government employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local clauses for conversion protections (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities have developed local clauses addressing turnover cooperation, strike contingency plans, price reductions for nonavailability or substandard performance, unbalanced bid evaluation, and manning level requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: clause requiring contractor cooperation in turnover/phase-in; clause requiring strike contingency plan; reduction in price tied to Inspection of Services clause; unbalanced bid evaluation clause to declare buy-ins non-responsive; clause requiring use of same number of personnel as proposed in step one. Legality/enforceability of some local clauses may be questionable but used in absence of specific DAR coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-aside and 8(a) procedures and coordination with SBA
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular and DOD/Navy directives encourage small and disadvantaged business use, but 8(a) negotiations with SBA can be complex and SBA reps may request in-house estimate access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide in-house estimate during negotiations; follow higher authority if SBA demands access. Historically, guidance evolved: 8(a) offers should not be solicited simultaneously with firm/bid competitions; SBA development monies are excluded from cost comparison. Check CNM/OFPP guidance for current rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when 8(a) offers vs in-house estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: If an 8(a) offer is received and the Government in-house estimate is lower, resolicitation under small business restricted advertising or unrestricted solicitation may be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CNM guidance (Aug 1979) clarified that requirements processed under 8(a) require further solicitation if in-house estimate is lower; original small-business set-aside solicitations need not be resolicited if in-house estimate is lower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid simultaneous firm/bid solicitations with 8(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competitive offers using the firm/bid rule should not be solicited at the same time as those requested from SBA under Section 8(a) procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent solicitations create procedural conflict and have been disallowed by higher authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prebid/Preproposal conferences and site visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers may be responsible for conducting prebid/preproposal conferences and site visits and must explain cost procedures to be applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some offices make conferences and site-visits mandatory (including for remote locations). Contracting Officer needs detailed familiarity with cost estimate and comparison procedures. Contractors often want explanations of methodologies, bid/performance bonds, and treatment of existing personnel in performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain cost differentials and conversion vs new-start treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Preproposal material should explain in detail cost differentials used depending on whether the function is a conversion or a new start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For conversions, the correct threshold for award may require total savings at least equal to 10% of Government personnel costs. Failure to explain these differentials can mislead contractors during conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide product samples at conference when service produces a product
rubrics_metrics.description: If the service results in a product, have a sample produced by the Government available for review at the prebid/preproposal conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A product sample helps bidders understand performance expectations and reduces ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control informal communications and site visits to preserve integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid informal communications by prospective bidders without Contracting Office representation; Contracting Officer should control site visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized information exchange can give unfair advantage and lead to disputes over whether verbal or written contract documents govern performance. Prospective offerers should not be permitted to review sites or receive information without contracting office knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Government as an offeror when solicitation amendments occur
rubrics_metrics.description: If solicitation amendments are required, the Government should be treated exactly as another offeror; procedures should include distributing amendments to the Task Group Chairperson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes at preproposal conferences may necessitate amendments; include Task Group Chairperson on amendment distribution and treat clarifications through Chairperson to preserve integrity and comparability among offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifications & changes must be routed through Task Group Chairperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for 'Clarifications' or similar questions must be referred to the Task Group Chairperson through the Contracting Officer, even if Formal Advertising is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive changes/clarifications can result in 'apples and oranges' comparisons; ensure Government in-house estimate is updated to reflect changes to maintain integrity of comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of competition for price comparison (DAR four conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Price competition exists if (1) at least two responsible offerors, (2) who can satisfy requirements, (3) independently contend for contract to award to lowest evaluated price, (4) by submitting priced offers responsive to solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition can be used to characterize the Government as an offeror for price competition purposes; consideration needed whether a single noncompetitive proposal is satisfactory for cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and entry of low contract price into cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officer is responsible for entering the 'Contract Price' on the cost comparison form (line 10) and determining the low contract price for the comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some contracting personnel are uncertain how to enter figures for incentive or cost-type contracts; the only available published guidance found by the researcher is in the Cost Comparison Handbook, so Contracting Officers should consult it for specific pricing arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor policy changes and message traffic for dynamic guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The program and associated policy guidance are dynamic; significant policy changes or implementing guidance may arrive via messages and not all directives will be updated promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers should check message traffic daily and be aware that some implementing directives may not yet reflect latest changes (e.g., NAVSUP/CNM messages).
